items.stem:

items.answer: (i) Hundi, part of the indigenous banking system. (ii) Safe transfer of money over long distances without carrying cash; credit for trade (payment could be deferred).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Hundi, part of the indigenous banking system. (ii) Safe transfer of money over long distances without carrying cash; credit for trade (payment could be deferred).

items.stem: Distinguish between profession and employment on the basis of code of conduct, capital investment, mode of establishment and reward or return.

items.stem: Which type of hundi is described? In each case give a reason. (i) A trader in ancient Varanasi issued a hundi that could be paid to any person, with no liability attached. (ii) A hundi was payable only after ninety days from its date.
items.answer: (i) Dhani-jog: A hundi payable to anyone with no liability is dhani-jog. (ii) Muddati: Payable after a specified period.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Dhani-jog (ii) Muddati

items.stem: Sahil works as an accounts clerk in Menon Agencies and gets a fixed salary every month. (i) Identify the economic activity. (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Employment: Working for another for salary under a service contract. (ii) Any two of: appointment letter and service agreement; reward is salary or wages; fixed and regular pay with little or no risk; no capital is required; norms of behaviour are laid down by the employer
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: appointment letter and service agreement; reward is salary or wages; fixed and regular pay with little or no risk; no capital is required; norms of behaviour are laid down by the employer

items.stem: Which of the following is true of profession but not of employment?
items.answer: Nature of work: rendering of personalised, expert services
items.markingKey: (c) profession: Nature of work: rendering of personalised, expert services. The other options describe employment.
options: Reward or return: salary or wages
Nature of work: performing work as per the service contract or rules of service
Nature of work: rendering of personalised, expert services
Risk: fixed and regular pay; no or little risk

items.stem: Banerjee and Sons produces woollens all year but sells them mainly in winter. Which auxiliary to trade removes the hindrance here? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Warehousing. Warehousing removes the hindrance of time.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Warehousing; 2 marks for the justification: Warehousing removes the hindrance of time.

items.stem: Which business activity is described here? "Activities such as transport, banking, insurance, warehousing and advertising that help trade."
items.answer: Auxiliaries to trade
items.markingKey: (d) Auxiliaries to trade: Activities such as transport, banking, insurance, warehousing and advertising that help trade.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the features of non-economic activities?
items.answer: Profit earning
items.markingKey: (d) "Profit earning" is one of the characteristics of business, not one of the features of non-economic activities.
options: Done out of love or affection

items.stem: A trader in ancient Varanasi issued a hundi that could be paid to any person, with no liability attached. Which type of hundi is described? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Dhani-jog. A hundi payable to anyone with no liability is dhani-jog.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Dhani-jog; 2 marks for the justification: A hundi payable to anyone with no liability is dhani-jog.

items.stem:
Rohan wants to open a leather bags shop. He has ₹8 lakh, has not decided whether to take a partner, and is choosing between a busy market in Guwahati and a cheaper place outside the city.
(i) Identify three basic factors he must consider. (ii) What should he weigh while choosing the location?
items.answer: (i) Choice of form of ownership, location of the enterprise, financing the proposition (also size of the firm). (ii) Nearness to customers and suppliers, transport, rent and cost, competition.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Choice of form of ownership, location of the enterprise, financing the proposition (also size of the firm). (ii) Nearness to customers and suppliers, transport, rent and cost, competition.
